vocab.english: [negates a verb in the past — 'did not']
[negates a verb in the future — 'will not']

patterns.exampleEnglish: I did not go to school yesterday.
patterns.grammarNote: لَمْ negates a verb in the PAST — but it does this by pairing with the present-tense form you already know, not the suffixed past-tense forms from levels 22-29. أَذْهَبُ becomes أَذْهَبْ after لَمْ (the final vowel just drops), which looks and sounds almost the same and means exactly the same thing in this app's exercises, since diacritics aren't shown anyway. So you don't need to learn new verb forms for this — just put لَمْ in front of a present-tense verb you already know, and it means 'didn't'. This is a third way to negate, alongside لَيْسَ/لَسْتُ (level 10, for is/am-not sentences) and the suffixed past tense (levels 22-29, for a positive statement of what did happen).

patterns.exampleEnglish: I will not go to school tomorrow.
patterns.grammarNote: لَنْ works the same way as لَمْ, but for the FUTURE: 'will not'. Arabic has no separate future-tense verb forms to learn here — لَنْ (and, for a positive future, سَـ or سَوْفَ, not covered yet) simply pairs with the present tense you already know. Between لَمْ (level 32, past), the present tense itself (levels 12-18, present/ongoing), and لَنْ (future), you can now talk about all three time frames using verb forms you've already drilled.
